$comment: Artifact id -> name tables for artifacts[] / accessories[] in export-schema.json. Static game metadata, not account data: these ids mean the same thing on every account. Published here because the payload carries opaque ints and nothing in it says what they mean - the same reason role-names.json exists. Read live off game build 11.67.0 (RslCompanionExtraction, `BlessingProbe --vaultenums`), and every table records how it was corroborated, because two of them replace tables that were WRONG until 2026-08-02.

kinds.$comment: The SLOT, from the game's IL2CPP `ArtifactKindId` enum. Decides which array a record lands in: 1-6 are gear (artifacts[]), 7-9 accessories (accessories[]). CORRECTION: schemas 7-8 of export-schema.md published a different and incorrect order (1 Weapon, 2 Helmet, 3 Shield, 4 Gauntlets, 5 Chestplate) - a consumer that hard-coded those labels is mislabelling slots. Corroborated independently of the enum by which primary stat each slot always rolls across a 5,820-piece vault: slot 1 is Health on all 420, slot 5 Attack on all 485, slot 6 Defence on all 517, slot 4 Speed on 388 of 516. Those are the game's fixed helmet/weapon/shield/boots primaries.
kinds.source: IL2CPP enum ArtifactKindId + per-slot primary-stat histogram

values.name: Cloak
values.note: The enum calls it Cloak; the UI labels it Amulet.

statKinds.$comment: `primaryBonus.statKindId` and `secondaryBonuses[].statKindId`, from the IL2CPP `StatKindId` enum. NOTE there is no separate id for the percentage form of a stat - one stat kind, and the bonus record's `isAbsolute` says whether its `value` is a flat amount or a fraction. (An older table in the extraction engine encoded 1 Health / 4 Health% / 7 Speed / 8 Critical Rate as distinct ids; that scheme is not what the game uses and was removed.) Corroborated by the same per-slot histogram as `kinds`.

values.name: CriticalHeal
values.note: Declared by the enum; never observed on an artifact (champion-only stat). Ids 1-8 are what artifacts roll.

ranks.$comment: `rankId` - the piece's stars, from the IL2CPP `ArtifactRankId` enum (One..Six). 0 = Unknown is declared but never observed.

rarities.$comment: `rarityId`. WEAKER PROVENANCE than the tables above, stated plainly: no IL2CPP enum was found under any of the names probed (ArtifactRarityId, ArtifactRarity, RarityId, Rarity, ItemRarityId), so these are the uploader's long-standing labels, supported only by the observed value range (1-6 across 5,820 pieces) matching the game's six quality tiers in order. Treat the ids as authoritative and the names as a convenience.

sets.$comment: `setKindId` for ids 0-66 - the artifact SET. 0 means NO SET, a real value and a common one (905 of 2,969 accessories carry it). Resolved from the game's own localized strings (key `l10n:artifact-set/name?id=N#static` -> the localized String beside it), and every name is paired with a description that agrees with it (1 Life <-> '2 Set: HP +15%'), which is what makes this trustworthy rather than merely plausible. NOTE `setKindId` is OVERLOADED: ids 1000-1004 in the same field are not sets at all - see accessoryEffects below. CORRECTION: everything published before 2026-08-02 was wrong from id 4 onward (it read 4 Critical Rate / 5 Accuracy / 6 Speed where the game says 4 Speed / 5 Critical Rate / 6 Crit Damage, and 47 Stone Skin where the game says 47 Protection with Stone Skin at 48). It had looked corroborated because the ids it skipped were absent from a 5,820-piece vault - a coincidence of one account's holdings, not evidence, and the lesson is that absence from one inventory says nothing about whether an id exists. Two entries are qualified: 9's own name string does not resolve, so `Lifesteal` is inferred from its description ('4 Set: Heals by 30% of damage dealt') and its position between Resistance and Fury - the only inferred entry here; 55 and 56 exist but this client build ships untranslated placeholder text for them, so they are omitted rather than named from a placeholder. Set BONUSES and piece counts are not here - that catalog belongs in RslCompanionMetadata, joined on this id.

accessoryEffects.$comment: `setKindId` 1000-1004 - NOT sets, despite sharing the field. Their l10n descriptions carry no piece count and no 'N Set:' prefix; each describes what one item does on its own. They occur on 76 of 2,969 accessories and on NO gear, across all three accessory slots, while accessories otherwise use the same 0-66 set ids gear uses. So a record's setKindId is either a set id or an accessory-effect id, and a consumer grouping 'by set' must exclude this range or it will invent five sets that do not exist. JOIN ON THE ID, NEVER THE NAME: Cleansing, Bloodshield, Reaction and Revenge all collide with names that have appeared in set tables elsewhere, including this repo's own previous (incorrect) one.

values.name: Refresh
values.effect: 5% chance to prevent a Skill going on cooldown after use

values.name: Cleansing
values.effect: 8% chance to remove 1 random debuff from the wearer each turn

values.name: Bloodshield
values.effect: Gives wearer Shield worth 5% of damage dealt after attacking

values.name: Reaction
values.effect: 25% chance to change critical hit into normal hit when attacked before the first turn each round
